# Findings this repository accepts, one per line, as
#
#     path | rule-id | sha256 fingerprint | reason
#
# All four fields are required and the reason is checked for being one. An
# entry that matches no finding FAILS the build: a suppression whose finding
# has gone is a decision nobody has re-read, and this repository already
# decided what to do about a list of known exceptions -- gate it, so the day
# one clears, the build says which. deploy/observability/alerts does the same
# thing to its unloaded alerts, for the same reason.
#
# THE PATH IS EXACT AND NEVER A GLOB. A glob is how a suppression arrives for
# a file nobody has written yet, and a file that arrives pre-suppressed is
# this repository's most-repeated failure -- a gate that quietly stops
# covering the newest surface -- with the paperwork already filled in.
#
# THE RULE IS NAMED, so an entry silences one class and not the file. The
# compose file is allowed to carry Section 14.1's local database default; it
# is not thereby allowed to carry a GitHub token.
#
# THE FINGERPRINT IS A HASH AND NOT THE VALUE, and the reason is not
# confidentiality -- every value below is already in the tree in plain sight.
# It is that this file must not become a SECOND place a credential is
# written. A second copy is the copy that outlives the rotation of the first,
# and a credential in two places is a credential nobody can retire. It is
# also why a reason must not quote the value it is about: this file is walked
# like every other, and a reason carrying the literal would report itself.
#
# The fingerprint is printed beside every finding, so adding an entry is
# reading the failure and writing down why -- never guessing at a digest.
#
# There is NO inline pragma and there never will be. CLAUDE.md's argument
# against an inline suppression is that it is a decision written where nobody
# re-reads it; a suppression that has to travel to this file is one somebody
# had to look at twice.


# --- The gate's own positive controls -------------------------------------
#
# test_secret_scan.py holds one literal of each provider's published shape,
# because a positive control has to be the thing it controls for. Every value
# here is invented and belongs to nobody. They are the reason this file is
# the length it is, and they are also the demonstration that it works.

.github/secret-scan/test_secret_scan.py | private-key-block | 8bcac7908eb9 | Positive control for the RSA PEM header. A header, not key material.

# --- Section 14.1's local development defaults ----------------------------
#
# CLAUDE.md names this exception outright and argues it: the compose defaults
# are what make a first `docker compose up` work with no prior setup, and the
# environment variable in front of each is the seam that keeps them out of
# anything deployed. docs/secrets.md tabulates the same four.
#
# THE SEAM IS AGAINST DEPLOYING THE VALUE, NOT AGAINST WRITING IT DOWN, which
# is why these are entries here rather than a shape the patterns skip. Every
# site the local database default is written appears below, and that is the
# useful half: rotating it is then a reconciliation this file enumerates,
# which is the one rule this repository has.

# --- The frozen record ----------------------------------------------------
#
# docs/superpowers is a historical record and CLAUDE.md forbids editing a
# plan to match the code that followed it. So a value printed in one is
# accepted where it is, and pinned by fingerprint so the file staying frozen
# is something this gate can see rather than something it assumes.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-07-pr06-compose.md | env-assignment | 8a11e54d9d5b | PR-06's frozen plan, printing the local database default it introduced.

# --- Prose and comments about the redactor --------------------------------
#
# Section 13.4's redactor is a component whose whole subject is the shape of a
# credential, so its chapter, its source comments and its suite are full of
# the shape being described. These are the residue the scanner cannot tell
# from the thing itself, and they are why the value rules end at whitespace,
# a parenthesis and a backtick rather than at the end of the line.

docs/backend-architecture/13-observability.md | connection-string-password | b988560af286 | Section 13.4's prose describing the shape, not carrying one.
docs/backend-architecture/13-observability.md | connection-string-password | f52fbd32b2b3 | The chapter's throwaway example of a value the redactor catches.
src/BuildingBlocks/Common.Web/SensitiveDataRedactor.cs | connection-string-password | 6d1d272cf2a9 | A comment showing the shape the redactor is written to find.
src/BuildingBlocks/Common.Web/SensitiveKeys.cs | connection-string-password | c0f68a414c0e | A doc comment arguing that the separator may carry spaces.

# rather than a silent substitution -- which is the whole reason the entry
# names a digest instead of a file.
